r0-context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-crew.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas if present: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, plus the handoff, the diff, and the relevant packet. r0-context.finding: Read global-crew.md, global-everyone.md (incl. §Verify claimed side-effects, §Scoped nulls), CREW_CONTEXT.md (incl. r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: MEASUREMENT.md executes the handoff's re-derivation task and mostly succeeds (DC1 machine assertion verified, MCP-arm counts independently reproduced exactly, corrections mostly real and correctly signed, far-side detector proven non-trivially capable of firing, dc6-mcp/dc6b-mcp UNMEASURED-vs-measured split verified correct). BUT: independent hand-recount of rep2-cli (r7/r10 detail) finds the reported 18 invocation attempts / 2 absorbable fumbles is WRONG under the write-up's own stated counting unit -- a shell for-loop in one Bash tool_use actually invoked checklist_engine.py 6 times (visible as 6 distinct 'usage: checklist_engine.py <subcmd>' blocks in the tool_result), but score_arm.py's engine_invocations() counts only static occurrences of the string 'checklist_engine.py' in the command text (=1 for that call), undercounting by 5. True rep2-cli = 23 attempts / 7 fumbles, not 18/2. This is a number that does not re-derive -- per the handoff's own governing rule this is a BLOCK.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: Reviewer stayed read/verify-only inside the f-424 worktree; did not rerun any of the four measurement arms or the DC6 arms. All independent verification was either (a) parsing existing record.jsonl files by hand/script, or (b) exercising score_arm.py against a small synthetic fixture I authored in the scratchpad to positive-control the far-side detector -- this tests the SCORER's mechanism only, not a re-run of an arm, and is exactly the kind of check the handoff asked for (criterion 6 / DC3-positive-control analogy). No arm was re-dispatched via claude -p.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Raw records (record.jsonl), scorer (score_arm.py), DC1 assertion (assert_dc1.py), fixture builder (make_arm.py), runner (run_arm.sh), and per-arm score.json/spine.json/step*.txt artifacts are all present under evidence/g4-dc5/ exactly as MEASUREMENT.md describes, and are dated together (Aug 9 16:14-16:27) with the arm directories, consistent with one measurement session. Evidence genuinely demonstrates the claimed behavior (agents drove the byte-identical spine to DONE through each interface) -- the defect found is in the SCORER's arithmetic (see r1-handoff/r7/r10), not in evidence presence or authenticity.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: MEASUREMENT.md follows CREW_CONTEXT.md's Verification Discipline in spirit (states scope, reports a negative as a complete result, names exact re-derivation commands) and constellation-how-to-talk (clear, direct, one name per thing). One violation of CREW_CONTEXT's own rule found during this review: 'A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed' -- score_arm.py's engine-invocation counter (a Bash command containing the literal substring 'checklist_engine.py' N times = N invocations) was never positive-controlled against a batched/looped shell command, which is exactly the shape that broke it (see r7/r10). No test fixture in evidence/g4-dc5/ exercises the counter against anything but literal, non-looped command text.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No architecture/structural-baseline divergence: this gate produces a measurement write-up and disposable scratch fixtures (evidence/g4-dc5/), not a shipped code change to the door or engine. Nothing here requires Cartographer reconciliation. Triage candidate logged separately: score_arm.py's engine_invocations() should count invocations per actual execution, not per static substring occurrence, so it does not silently undercount any future looped/batched CLI command -- flagged as an out-of-scope fix, not applied here.

r7-independent-recount.title: Independent recount of one arm's attempts/fumbles
r7-independent-recount.imperative: Do NOT just re-run score_arm.py and call it confirmed. Independently parse at least one arm's record.jsonl (own script or by hand) and state whether you got the same invocation-attempt and fumble counts as MEASUREMENT.md.
r7-independent-recount.finding: Wrote my own independent parse of record.jsonl (not reusing score_arm.py's function) for all 4 arms. MCP arms (rep1-mcp, rep2-mcp): counted tool_use names by simple dict-count of the mcp__spine__* prefix -- got 19 and 17, matching MEASUREMENT.md exactly. CLI arms: counted occurrences of the literal string 'checklist_engine.py' per Bash command and summed -- got 21 (rep1-cli) and 18 (rep2-cli), which superficially MATCHES the reported numbers. BUT this naive method is the same static-text method score_arm.py itself uses, so agreement with it proves nothing beyond 'both regexes agree' (the CREW_CONTEXT trap: 're-running the same check twice is not independent verification'). I went one level deeper and read the actual tool_result TEXT for every CLI Bash call. rep2-cli's 3rd command is 'for cmd in claim start attest advance record release; do ... checklist_engine.py  --help ...; done' -- a shell loop. The tool_result contains 6 distinct 'usage: checklist_engine.py <subcmd>' blocks (verified: one per subcommand, pasted in full in my working notes), proving the engine was actually invoked 6 times. Static substring counting sees 'checklist_engine.py' once in that command's source text and credits only 1 invocation + 1 usage-read. True count for that one Bash call is 6 invocations / 6 usage-reads, not 1/1. Corrected rep2-cli = 23 invocation attempts (18+5) / 7 absorbable fumbles (2+5), not the reported 18/2. rep1-cli's own multi-invocation command (4 literal, non-looped lines each mentioning checklist_engine.py once) was checked the same way and DOES match (4 usage blocks for 4 literal mentions) -- so only the looped command is wrong. VERDICT: I could NOT re-derive rep2-cli's reported number from the raw record by true independent means. Per the handoff's explicit governing rule ('A number you cannot re-derive is a BLOCK') this is a BLOCK finding.

r8-counting-unit-parity.title: Counting-unit parity across arms
r8-counting-unit-parity.imperative: Confirm the CLI arm's compound Bash commands are counted as n invocations (not 1), that the MCP arm is not advantaged/disadvantaged by the unit choice, and state whether the chosen unit is honestly applied end to end.
r8-counting-unit-parity.finding: The DESIGN is sound and honestly stated: CLI Bash commands are meant to count as N invocations (engine_invocations() counts occurrences of 'checklist_engine.py'), MCP calls count as exactly 1 each by construction (a typed tool call carries one verb, cannot batch). For 3 of 4 arms this parity holds and I verified it by independent recount (r7). For rep2-cli it does NOT hold in practice: a shell for-loop batches 6 invocations into text that only mentions the engine binary once, so the implementation's counting mechanism silently breaks unit parity exactly where CLI batching is most aggressive (6-way batching, more than the disclosed batching-correction's own worked example of 3-4x). The chosen unit (one invocation attempt, however packaged) is the right one in principle; the implementation does not honor it for loop-packaged batches. This is the same underlying defect as r7, recorded again here because it is specifically a parity violation, not just a wrong number.

r9-client-rejected-corroboration.title: Client-rejected calls counted; server log corroboration-only
r9-client-rejected-corroboration.imperative: Confirm client-rejected calls are counted from record.jsonl and that mcp_calls.jsonl is used only as corroboration, never as the numerator.
r9-client-rejected-corroboration.finding: Read score_arm.py in full: score() only ever opens arm_dir/record.jsonl (the driving agent's own client-side record); mcp_calls.jsonl (the server log) is never opened or referenced anywhere in score_arm.py or assert_dc1.py. Confirmed by grep: no reference to mcp_calls.jsonl in either script. Cross-checked rep1-mcp and rep2-mcp: client-observed mcp__spine__* tool_use count (19, 17) exactly equals mcp_calls.jsonl line count (19, 17) in this dataset -- i.e. no call was client-rejected before reaching the server in these particular runs, so the corroboration-only design was not empirically load-bearing here, but the code-level guarantee (server log never used as numerator) holds regardless of what this dataset happened to contain.

r10-disclosed-corrections.title: Disclosed corrections verified, both directions; hunt for an undisclosed third
r10-disclosed-corrections.imperative: Verify the batching correction (toward the door) and help-output correction (away from the door) are real, correctly applied, and correctly signed. Look hard for a third, undisclosed correction.
r10-disclosed-corrections.finding: Both disclosed corrections are real, correctly signed, and correctly described: (1) batching correction -- verified rep1-cli's 21 invocations vs 10 tool_calls_carrying_them independently (r7), correctly moves the CLI number UP/toward the door being credited fairly rather than penalized for batching -- correct direction. (2) help-output correction -- verified the SHAPE_RE patterns (e.g. 'usage: checklist_engine') would otherwise match a --help block's own usage text, and the code's 'if u: s = 0' zeroes shape-error count whenever a help/usage marker is present, moving the CLI arm's fumble count DOWN/against the door -- correct direction, confirmed by reading the actual --help output text for rep1-cli and rep2-cli. HOWEVER, hunting for an undisclosed third correction (as instructed) surfaced one: the engine_invocations() counting mechanism itself contains an undisclosed, unintentional THIRD adjustment -- static substring-counting of Bash command text silently undercounts any shell-loop-packaged batch of invocations (see r7). This is not stated anywhere in MEASUREMENT.md's 'Two corrections made to the unit mid-measurement' section, which claims exactly two. It is not a deliberate methodological correction like the other two (no stated rationale, no disclosed direction) -- it is an uncaught implementation bug that happens to move rep2-cli's numbers DOWN (against the door, in the 'attempts' reading) but also suppresses evidence of one of the door's biggest per-arm advantages. Because it is silent rather than disclosed and reasoned-about like the other two, and because it moves a headline number, this is graded fail: the write-up's claim of exactly-two-corrections is incomplete.

r11-order-practice-effects.title: Order/practice effects controlled vs merely acknowledged
r11-order-practice-effects.imperative: State whether running both orders (rep1 CLI-first, rep2 MCP-first) plus cold agents actually neutralises practice transfer, or whether the claim is overstated.
r11-order-practice-effects.finding: Cold-agent-per-arm construction (each arm is a fresh claude -p dispatch on its own fresh spine copy) genuinely rules out the agent itself carrying learning across arms -- verified via make_arm.py (each arm gets shutil.rmtree + fresh spine build) and run_arm.sh (each is an independent timeout 900 claude -p dispatch with no shared state). The only channel order could act through is MY fixture-building consistency across reps, which MEASUREMENT.md names honestly ('the order that remains controlled for is mine, not the agents'') rather than overclaiming full neutralization -- this is an honest, correctly-scoped claim, not an overclaim. With the r7 correction applied, both orders still agree in DIRECTION (CLI costs more invocation-attempts than MCP in both rep1 [21 vs 19] and rep2 [23 vs 17, corrected]) though MAGNITUDE now differs more between orders (+2 vs +6) than MEASUREMENT.md's 'agree in direction and magnitude' implies -- a minor overclaim on magnitude once r7's correction is applied, worth a wording fix but not a blocker on its own.

r12-far-side-detector.title: Far-side recovery detector: could it have fired at all
r12-far-side-detector.imperative: Verify the far-side detector is not structurally incapable of firing (positive control). If it cannot fire, that is a BLOCK regardless of the reported zero.
r12-far-side-detector.finding: Positive-controlled the detector directly (scratchpad synthetic record.jsonl, NOT a rerun of any arm): a Bash tool_use containing a shape-error-triggering engine call, followed by a Read tool_use, correctly scores far_side_recoveries=1 -- the mechanism is not structurally incapable of firing. HOWEVER it has a real, undisclosed, arm-asymmetric blind spot: INSPECT_TOOLS = {Read, Grep, Glob} excludes Bash. The CLI arm's --allowedTools is 'Bash Write Read' (from run_arm.sh) -- across both CLI reps, Read was called only once (rep2-cli) and zero times (rep1-cli); Bash was the CLI arm's dominant/near-exclusive tool (11 of ~12-15 calls each). A second synthetic control confirms: a shape-error via Bash followed by a Bash-based inspection (e.g. 'cat spine.json') is COMPLETELY invisible to the detector -- not counted as far_side, not counted as anything. So for the CLI arm specifically, the detector can only see recovery through a tool the CLI arm almost never uses. Separately and more fundamentally: in the ACTUAL data, shape_errors=0 and other_errors=0 in all 4 arms, so prev_failed never became True anywhere -- the far-side channel had zero real trigger events to react to in this entire dataset, regardless of tool coverage. So 'zero far-side recoveries' is true but UNTESTED by this measurement: it reflects 'no failures occurred' (itself a genuine finding, consistent with DC1's zero-malformed-calls result), not 'failures occurred and were not followed by recovery'. Graded pass because the detector is demonstrably capable of firing (not structurally incapable, the literal BLOCK trigger in the handoff) and MEASUREMENT.md's own text ('it simply was not there to move') already concedes this rather than overclaiming a tested null. Recommend disclosing the Bash blind spot and the zero-trigger-events caveat explicitly if this instrument is reused on a task shape with real failures.

This is genuinely UNMEASURED: the engine's own freshness check refused the stale reading, so no threshold instruction was ever emitted and the agent's drive-to-DONE says nothing about compliance. dc6b-mcp/gauge.json observed_at 23:24:10.742588Z (written after re-claim); its 150KB record.jsonl contains exactly 2 of 33 tool_results carrying the full arrival instruction verbatim -- matching MEASUREMENT.md's '2 of 33' claim exactly on independent parse. Neither direction of the failure mode named in the handoff is present: dc6-mcp is not a measured negative dressed as unmeasured (it is genuinely unmeasured -- no instruction ever arrived), and dc6b-mcp is not an unmeasured condition dressed as a measured negative (it has 2 real arrivals plus a clear, verified action+non-compliance sequence). Both land on the correct side.

r15-dc1-machine-assertion.imperative: Confirm assert_dc1.py runs over the same records DC5 draws from and would fail if either half (reached_done, zero malformed calls) were untrue.
r15-dc1-machine-assertion.finding: assert_dc1.py (read in full) calls score() from the same score_arm.py module MEASUREMENT.md's DC5 numbers come from, over rep1-mcp/rep2-mcp -- the identical records, not a re-telling. It fails (returns 1, appends to failures[]) if reached_done is False OR shape_errors is nonzero, for either arm -- both halves genuinely gate the assertion, verified by reading the conditional logic directly. Re-ran the exact command from the handoff: 'rep1-mcp: reached_done=True malformed_calls=0 invocation_attempts=19', 'rep2-mcp: reached_done=True malformed_calls=0 invocation_attempts=17', 'DC1 PASS... EXIT=0' -- output matches MEASUREMENT.md verbatim. DC1 is unaffected by the rep2-cli miscount (r7) since it only reads the MCP arms, which do not use Bash/shell loops and cannot exhibit the same undercount by construction (one typed tool call = one verb, always).

r16-dc6-verdict-split.title: DC6 verdict split: arrival/action PASS, stop-ignored attribution
r16-dc6-verdict-split.imperative: Check DC6's arrival and action claims against dc6b-mcp/record.jsonl directly, and judge whether attributing the ignored 'and stop' half to agent-compliance behaviour (not a door defect) is correct.
r16-dc6-verdict-split.finding: Read dc6b-mcp/record.jsonl directly. Arrival: confirmed verbatim at 2 of 33 tool_results (r14). Action: confirmed -- after the FIRST arrival, the agent's sequence includes some intervening precondition-refused attempts (spine_start x2, one failed advance -- these are engine STATE refusals, not fumbles, consistent with the disclosed exclusion) before successfully attaching a refresh-request and then a --why advance; MEASUREMENT.md's phrase 'the agent's very next calls were...' slightly overstates the immediacy (there were 4 intervening calls, not zero) but the qualitative claim -- both named actions were taken -- is correct. Stop-ignored: confirmed by reading the full remaining trace -- the agent attached fresh refresh-requests at m1 through m4 and drove all the way to DONE, releasing the lease at the very end, exactly as MEASUREMENT.md describes. Attribution judgment: agreeing this is agent-compliance behaviour rather than a door defect is correct -- the door (MCP tool result) delivered the 'and stop' instruction intact and verbatim (confirmed in the arrival text I read), so the door did its job; what happened after is the driving agent's decision, outside the door's control. Minor wording note (not a blocker): 'very next calls' should be 'next successful calls' or similar.

consolidation.summary: Re-derivation fails its own governing rule ('a number you cannot re-derive is a BLOCK'). Independent hand-parse of rep2-cli's record.jsonl (r7, r8) shows the reported 18 invocation-attempts / 2 absorbable-fumbles is wrong: a 6-way shell for-loop was scored as 1 invocation because score_arm.py's counter matches static substring occurrences of 'checklist_engine.py' in Bash command TEXT rather than actual runtime executions. True rep2-cli = 23 attempts / 7 fumbles. This also means MEASUREMENT.md's claim of exactly two disclosed mid-measurement corrections (r10) is incomplete -- a third, undisclosed, unintentional adjustment is baked into the counting instrument itself, and it is load-bearing: corrected CLI-arm attempt counts [21,23] no longer overlap MCP's [19,17] at all, which changes the strength (though not the small-n caveats) of the DC5 finding materially from what is printed. Everything else independently re-derives cleanly: DC1's machine assertion (r15), the MCP-arm counts (r7, exact match), the client-rejected/corroboration-only design (r9), the batching and help-output corrections' direction and correctness (r10, apart from the missing third), order/cold-agent controls (r11), the far-side detector's capability to fire at all via a positive control though with an undisclosed Bash blind spot for the CLI arm (r12), the dc6-mcp/dc6b-mcp UNMEASURED-vs-measured split (r14), and the DC6 arrival/action/stop-ignored attribution (r16). This is NOT a block on the unflattering-negative conclusion itself (the honest-null clause is honored on the numbers as printed, r13) -- it is a block because the printed numbers are not what the raw record supports for one of the four arms, and that arm is one of only two data points backing the CLI side of the headline comparison.

triage_candidates.statement: score_arm.py's engine_invocations() counts static occurrences of the substring 'checklist_engine.py' in a Bash command's SOURCE TEXT, not actual runtime executions. A shell for-loop (rep2-cli's claim/start/attest/advance/record/release --help loop) mentions the string once but executes the engine 6 times; the counter credits 1. Fix: either (a) forbid/discourage loop-packaged invocations in run_arm.sh's prompt and re-measure, or (b) count actual invocations from the tool_result text (e.g. count of distinct 'usage: checklist_engine.py <subcmd>' / RAIL: banner occurrences), and add a positive-control fixture (a synthetic record.jsonl with a known loop) asserting the scorer gets it right, per CREW_CONTEXT's 'a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed'. Re-score rep2-cli (and re-derive the DC5 means/spreads) once fixed.
